//: ARC install broker - package manifest.
This file is the ONLY authority the broker has. A request from the shell carries
an 'id' from this file and nothing else - never a URL, a path, or an argument.
Everything that gets downloaded or executed is named here, by an administrator.
Deployed to C:\ProgramData\ARC\packages.json, writable by administrators only.
The worker refuses to run if that stops being true.
Fields:
id           required. Slug the shell asks for. [a-z0-9._-], max 64 chars.
name         required. Human label for logs and the shell UI.
url          https:// only. The installer to fetch.
publisher    required with url. Substring that MUST appear in the downloaded
file's Authenticode signer subject. The signature must also be
Valid. This is the provenance pin - it survives vendor version
bumps, which a sha256 pin does not.
sha256       optional. Exact content pin. Use for installers that never change.
When present it is enforced IN ADDITION to the publisher check.
type         'exe' (default) or 'msi'.
args         argument array passed to the installer. Silent switches go here.
For msi the worker supplies /i /qn /norestart itself.
verifyPath   optional. Path that must exist afterwards for the install to be
reported OK, regardless of the installer's exit code.
wingetId     optional. If winget is present it is preferred over url. This
image has no winget, so it is unused here - kept so the same
manifest works on the laptop.
Adding an entry is a decision to let the console shell install that software
with nobody at the machine. Adding a wildcard, a caller-supplied url, or a
'skip verification' flag would hand arcshell the box. Don't.
